original_value: AbstractAs an important part of brain‐computer interface (BCI), the electroencephalography (EEG) technology of motor imagery (MI) has been gradually recognized for its great theoretical value and practical application. In this study, in view of the different MI tasks corresponding to active region of the EEG signals, we adopt a two‐dimensional form including time, frequency, and electrode location information, then we design a classification method containing continuous small convolutional neural network (CSCNN). This method is mainly used for feature extraction through continuous small convolutional kernels and one rectangle convolutional kernel, and the softmax classifier for classification. In the experiment, classification accuracy and kappa value are used as evaluation criteria to verify the effectiveness of the method proposed in this study. For classification accuracy, BCI competition IV data set 2b is used to compare with the other five classification methods (CNN, CNN‐SAE, stacked autoencoder [SAE], support vector machine [SVM], and one‐dimensional convolution combined with gated recurrent unit [1DCGRU]). The results demonstrate that the overall accuracy of CSCNN is higher than other methods, and CSCNN obtains an average accuracy of 82.8%. For kappa value, BCI competition IV data set 2b is used to compare with the other three methods (filter bank common spatial pattern [FBCSP], Twin SVM, and CNN‐SAE). The performance of CSCNN is better with an average value of 0.663. Overall, the results show that CSCNN maintains a small number of parameters and improves the classification accuracy.

result.paraphrase: As an important component of brain-computer interface (BCI) systems, motor imagery (MI) electroencephalography (EEG) has increasingly been recognized for its strong theoretical significance and practical value. In this study, considering that different MI tasks correspond to active regions of EEG signals, we use a two-dimensional representation incorporating time, frequency, and electrode-location information, and design a classification approach based on a continuous small convolutional neural network (CSCNN). The method primarily performs feature extraction with continuous small convolutional kernels and one rectangular convolutional kernel, followed by softmax classification. In experiments, classification accuracy and kappa value are used as evaluation metrics to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. For classification accuracy, BCI competition IV dataset 2b is used to compare CSCNN with five other methods (CNN, CNN-SAE, stacked autoencoder [SAE], support vector machine [SVM], and one-dimensional convolution combined with gated recurrent unit [1DCGRU]). The results show that CSCNN achieves higher overall accuracy than the other methods, with an average accuracy of 82.8%. For kappa value, BCI competition IV dataset 2b is used to compare it with three methods (filter bank common spatial pattern [FBCSP], Twin SVM, and CNN-SAE). CSCNN performs better, with an average value of 0.663. Overall, the results indicate that CSCNN keeps the number of parameters small while improving classification accuracy.
